channel.title: Lars van den Berg
channel.description: Writing on Europe, from the inside.

item.title: Galileo, Copernicus, and the Gap Between Sovereignty Rhetoric and Infrastructure Reality
item.description: On 7 April 2026, the European Commission published proposal COM(2026)152 to recast EUSPA as the European Union Space Services Agency, granting it a standalone legal basis decoupled from the 2021–2027 Multiannual Financial Framework.

item.title: Landsbergis at the Atlantic Council
item.description: On 6 May 2026, the Atlantic Council appointed Gabrielius Landsbergis — Lithuania's foreign minister from December 2020 to November 2024 — as co-chair of its Reimagining European Defense and Innovation Task Force.

item.title: Europe and the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: On 14 April 2026, the European Union and the United Kingdom announced EMAM-S — the European Maritime Awareness Mission in the Strait of Hormuz — a naval operation bringing together more than forty nations to protect commercial shipping through the world's most consequential energy chokepoint.

item.title: The Pact That Preserves What It Promised to Replace
item.description: On 12 June 2026, the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum enters full application — replacing Dublin III with the AMMR and activating new border procedures, screening rules, and a solidarity pool.

item.title: The Hague 5% Pledge: Verification by Design, Compliance by Faith
item.description: On 24–25 June 2025, NATO's 32 heads of state and government adopted the Hague Investment Plan: a commitment to spend 5% of GDP on defence and security by 2035.

item.title: A European Army Without a Legal Home
item.description: On 28 January 2026, EU Defence Commissioner Andrius Kubilius published speaking notes proposing a standing European force of 100,000 troops and a European Security Council of 10–12 permanent members to bypass unanimity in defence decisions.

item.title: Two Schengens, One Incoherent Policy: Russian Visas After the Ban
item.description: On 15 September 2025, Commissioner Magnus Brunner told the European Parliament that the European Union "does not have the ability to completely ban their issuance" — referring to Russian visas.

item.title: Greece's Financial Prosperity
item.description: In March 2025, Moody's upgraded Greece to Baa3, completing the country's return to investment grade across all three major credit agencies — S&P, Fitch, and Moody's.

item.title: The Empty Frontier: Europe's Eastern Border Strategy Meets Demographic Reality
item.description: On 18 February 2026, the European Commission published a Communication titled "Strong Eastern Regions, Safe Europe," addressing border regions across nine member states that share a frontier with Russia, Belarus, and Ukraine.

item.title: Treaty Architecture vs Coercion: Why Spain Survived Trump's Threats
item.description: On 2 March 2026, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez told the United States it could not use the bases at Rota and Morón for strikes on Iran. Within 48 hours, Donald Trump threatened to cut off all trade with Spain.

item.title: A Bilateral Hardening
item.description: On 25 April 2026, Emmanuel Macron and Kyriakos Mitsotakis renewed the Franco-Greek strategic defence partnership in Athens for another five years.

item.title: The Summit Problem
item.description: On April 27, six NATO sources — a senior European official and five diplomats — told Reuters the alliance is considering whether to stop holding annual leaders' summits.

item.title: Why Trump Will Lose the Midterms
item.description: Donald Trump's job approval sits at roughly 40%. Disapproval: 57%. These are not the numbers of a president whose party holds ground in midterms.

item.title: The Conditionality Test
item.description: On 29 April 2026, the European Parliament voted 418 to 207 to call on the European Commission to trigger the rule-of-law conditionality mechanism against Slovakia.

item.description: On 22 April 2026, POLITICO reported that the White House had compiled a "naughty and nice" list of NATO allies, sorted by their willingness to support the US-led war against Iran.

item.title: The Netherlands Builds Europe's First National Code Forge
item.description: On 24 April 2026, the Dutch government soft-launched code.overheid.nl — a self-hosted, Forgejo-based code platform for government open-source software. No EU member state has done this before.

item.title: The Pact Meets the Surge: EU Migration Rules Face the Iran Crisis
item.description: On 12 June 2026, the EU's Migration and Asylum Pact becomes operational law across all member states. Six weeks before that deadline, the system is about to meet a surge it was not built for.
